question: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre, took place in consequence to the protest against the _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rowlatt Act**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on 13th April 1919.
 
• It was a direct consequence of the widespread protests against the **Rowlatt Act**.
 
• The Rowlatt Act was passed by the British government in India in March 1919.
 
• This act allowed certain political cases to be tried without juries and permitted internment of suspects without trial.
 
• It led to widespread anger and protests among the Indian populace, which culminated in the tragic massacre.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre was carried out by troops under the command of General Dyer.
 
• It took place in Amritsar, Punjab, where a large crowd had gathered for a peaceful protest.
 
• General Dyer ordered his troops to fire into the crowd, resulting in hundreds of deaths and thousands of injuries.
 
• The massacre is considered a turning point in Indian history, galvanizing the Indian independence movement.
 
• It highlighted the brutal nature of British colonial rule and intensified the call for complete independence (Swaraj).
